players.note: Top offense, top talent - all time season potential
Concerns about the offense, but it was the same situation with Pennix last year. Ultimately, cannot fade him.
Upside with Burrow in this offense is immense.
People forget how dominant he was before he got hurt.
Always reliable, always good, plays through injury. Everything you could want from your first round pick.
He may face some regression - but he is also a top talent. This offense may be good not great, but he will still get his. Shaheed getting more involved should help open things up even further.
Could win you your league but I prefer JSN and Amon Ra for alphas without the question marks in RD1.
The SB MVP - he was the centerpiece of the offense on Monday. He showed why he is so good and the explosive upside in this offense. Jumps a tier immediately.
Workhorse in a top-5 scoring offense; safe with upside.

Age + injury history. Elite if healthy; not a first-round pick for me since I am more risk averse in first round. Playing it safe with an Amon Ra vs the risk of CMC - the risk here is lose your season. Amon Ra is stable and my preference.

He shut down all the concerns about the ankle and looked amazing. Everything I hoped for him last year. He may be ready for the second season leap and I have him back to where he was preseason for me. I just need to see it in a tougher matchup before he joins the next tier up.
Just had the single best TE season with Jacoby, everyone talking about Wilson and MHJ, but they don't go away from McBride.

Slow start to last season but then turned it on. To me, with Chase and Higgins, he does have potential to get phased about a bit more than other backs ahead, which is why I prefer them. He is as solid as they come though.
The player you never want to bet against, but he is getting up there in age. Father time is undefeated, and I fear taking young studs over him in case Father time, decides it is time.

Bounce back year coming. People forget he was a top tier at position prior to high ankle sprain. We know who he is, and he is going to remind everyone in a top offense that can sustain him and Pickens both.
A down year from Jefferson with "9" is not enough for me to forget that he is probably the best receiver in the NFL still. Kyler should be enough to launch him back into the upper echelon of ranks.
The best Fantasy QB consistently. Don't overthink this one, positional advantage.
He's going to get a ton of volume in an offense I expect to be better this year. Especially with Higgins out, he should get more.

In the brief audition he had of being the lone lead back, he crushed.. then got hurt. With OC in Mike McDaniels, he is in great hands. He may talk about hot hand, but we saw what he did with Achane. He's going to get his workhorse the ball. Could easily jump a tier if all goes right.
I think we get one last swan song from Saquon this year, and I feel like I am too low to be frank. New OC, and AJ Brown gone. They are going to need some vintage Saquon.
Really good this year especially without Tyson to start. He was the WR3 last year down the stretch.
RB1 in a Ben Johnson offense! Sign me up. We know Swift is talented, and I think he dominates especially as Monangai is week to week.

I think Achane is one of the probably 5 most talented backs in the league. This is not about him. Situationally, I hate this MIA offense. No WRs, a mobile QB who may not check down as much, and overall a questionable offense. He is still uncuttable because of who he is, but I am taking others over him for this reason.
Zay is solid - but I don't see him taking the leap. He doesn't score TDs which is the variable here. He is safe and the TD pendulum could swing his way. But I don't see it.

He is a top tier talent. But, he is coming off an ACL and lateral Meniscus. We have not seen that combo before. He has even admitted he is still regaining his feel. Mix in Matt Nagy as OC - and I am worried. I am willing to take the swing approaching the 4th round, but color me concerned.
An old flag plant - it feels good seeing him up the ranks! He is as solid and consistent as they come, workhorse in a good offense. Tier jump very possible.

High ankle sprain I think he will have a slow start to year. We know the talent though. Generational. We are getting a discount we wouldn't otherwise. Be okay with a slow start, to potentially have a league winner thereafter.
He really turned it up last season when Ceedee went down. While I project Ceedee to be the number 1 again, there is enough space in this offense for two alphas.

I am concerned about Gainwell and Tucker. Bucky is a smaller back, it was always the question, can he sustain the lead? I think Gainwell will take some valuable passing away from him, but ultimately, this was a back we drafted in round 2 last year. He is going too late.
Eagles demise is overstated, and Smith is an alpha. He is that good, and ready to step into the AJB shadow.
Lamar had a down year on the back of injuries and other variables. I consider it a fluke.
Much like Wilson, Breece transcended a terrible situation last year. I think it improves this year, and the Jets know it comes through these two players.
Bold: top-15 WR. Jets offense takes a step forward with Geno. Wilson was dominating last year even in one of the worst passing attacks ever. This should improve this year, and he stands to benefit.

Turf toe concern out of camp - if it was not for that, he would be higher. Turf Toe is one of those injuries I always balk at. And we saw last year how Egbuka struggled coming off injury. I am worried.
20 carries, 60 yards, two scores, 62% of Houston's carries. The metric's low on the efficiency; I'm ranking the role and the goal-line work.

The model loves Tee Higgins this year as the offense should crush. Let this be his ceiling. He is always hurt, if you told me he would play a full season, I would have him up a tier easily. I don't buy it, so for me he sits with Nabers at questions.

Kyren should be great, and it is a great offense. My projections and model, along with my gut, have Corum inching closer though. If there is a lapse, he may not give job back. But until then, Kyren is as solid as they come.
Model LOVES Parker. I had to drag him down to account for some of the risk. I think he crushes though. He has the work ethic, and he is playing for a contract. TLaw loves him also.
147 yards and two scores on 8 targets. Risk High is the knee history and a target tree with Golden at 12 and Kraft at 6.
Denver breakout offense; expect him to crush.

I want to rank Ladd higher, but I can't find myself doing it. Last season was a down year after his crazy rookie year. I worry though that he was outdone by Keenan last year, and Quentin takes some shine off. This offseason, I can't find them talking about him distinguishing himself like other camp hype. That worries me.
Top-2 TE. Kubiak OC gets guys open; 29% of targets
Middle-tier WR2, not the WR5 the volume implied. I am afraid to be wrong.

The lowest you may see London, but the model agrees. I am worried about this offense, and Tua as a starting QB. You may not like what you see, but his volume makes it harder to drop further to start. He could move up or down a tier quickly.
He may be the answer in this bears offense. They are going to score a ton of points, and he was the focal point down stretch last year. I think it continues, and he is a difference maker.
Couldn't ask for much of a better fit for AJB than Maye, as accurate as they get. Health and age are his only questions, but I think he has another good season in him.

A muddied backfield, and that is exactly where I want to take shots. Everyone wrote off Dobbins, everyone loves Jonah Coleman. Harvey probably has the best role of the three: the passing work and a nose for the end zone, in his second year in the offense. In an ambiguous backfield, he's my bet.
Allgeier out-carried him 17 to 11 in his debut off the ankle. I'm still above the model because the talent is the talent, but below where I was until the split reads differently.

Tuten is a talented, explosive back. I can see Chris Rodriguez stealing valuable touches, which is what the model is assuming, but when a backfield is in question I would rather draft the back with the upside. Second-year back, and I'm taking the swing.
8 carries for 15 with Warren getting the targets. The metric and I both see a 1B.
